compatibilityIssues: Migration from Web Forms to .NET 8 required
upgradeSteps: Refactor Web Forms to Razor Pages/MVC

issues.impact: Complete rewrite of data access layer required. All Entity Framework 6 DbContext code must be migrated to EF Core. Entity configurations using EntityTypeConfiguration<T> must be converted to IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>.
issues.description: The application uses EntityFramework 6.2.0 which is NOT compatible with .NET 8. Entity Framework 6.x is a .NET Framework-only library and cannot be used in .NET 8 applications.
issues.recommendation: Migrate to Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore 8.0.0 and Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer 8.0.0. All DbContext classes, entity configurations, and LINQ queries must be updated for EF Core compatibility.
issues.title: Entity Framework 6.2.0 is incompatible with .NET 8

issues.impact: All logging statements throughout the application need to be updated. Log configuration must move from log4Net.xml to appsettings.json or Program.cs.
issues.description: The application uses log4net 2.0.10 which is a legacy logging framework. While it may work, it's not the recommended approach for .NET 8 applications.
issues.recommendation: Migrate to Microsoft.Extensions.Logging with Serilog.AspNetCore 8.0.0. Replace all ILog references with ILogger<T>. Convert structured logging patterns.
issues.title: log4net 2.0.10 is legacy and not recommended for .NET 8

issues.impact: Major architectural change required. All System.Web dependencies must be identified and replaced with ASP.NET Core equivalents.
issues.description: The project references System.Web which is .NET Framework-only and does not exist in .NET 8. This is a fundamental incompatibility.
issues.recommendation: Remove System.Web references entirely. Replace with ASP.NET Core equivalents: HttpContext.Current → IHttpContextAccessor, Server.MapPath → IWebHostEnvironment, Session → distributed cache, Cache → IMemoryCache/IDistributedCache.
issues.title: System.Web reference is not compatible with .NET 8

issues.impact: Bundle configuration must be completely rewritten for ASP.NET Core.
issues.description: System.Web.Optimization is used for bundling and minification but is .NET Framework-only.
issues.recommendation: Replace with WebOptimizer or built-in ASP.NET Core bundling and minification. Migrate BundleConfig.cs to ASP.NET Core approach.
issues.title: System.Web.Optimization is not compatible with .NET 8

issues.impact: Complete redesign of application startup and request pipeline. Autofac DI configuration must move to built-in DI. Database initialization must move to Program.cs.
issues.description: Global.asax and HttpApplication lifecycle events (Application_Start, Application_BeginRequest, Session_Start) are Web Forms-specific and not available in ASP.NET Core.
issues.recommendation: Migrate application startup logic to Program.cs. Move Application_Start to WebApplication builder configuration. Convert Application_BeginRequest to middleware. Migrate Session_Start logic to session configuration or distributed cache.
issues.title: Global.asax application lifecycle not supported in .NET 8

issues.impact: DI container configuration must be completely rewritten for ASP.NET Core. Property injection used in Web Forms pages must be replaced with constructor injection.
issues.description: The application uses Autofac.Integration.Web which is designed for ASP.NET Web Forms and uses IContainerProviderAccessor pattern not compatible with ASP.NET Core.
issues.recommendation: Replace with built-in ASP.NET Core dependency injection or Autofac.Extensions.DependencyInjection for ASP.NET Core. Migrate ApplicationModule to service registration extension methods.
issues.title: Autofac.Integration.Web is Web Forms-specific

issues.impact: Every class using log4net must be updated. Static logger instances must be replaced with injected ILogger<T>.
issues.description: Log4net's LogManager.GetLogger pattern is used throughout the codebase and is incompatible with modern .NET logging.
issues.recommendation: Replace with ILogger<T> injected via constructor. Update all logging calls to use Microsoft.Extensions.Logging patterns.
issues.title: LogManager from log4net used throughout application

issues.impact: All code accessing HttpContext.Current must be refactored to use IHttpContextAccessor.
issues.description: The application uses HttpContext.Current which does not exist in ASP.NET Core. This pattern is used for accessing session and request information.
issues.recommendation: Inject IHttpContextAccessor to access HttpContext. Use HttpContext.Session with proper session configuration. Consider moving session state to distributed cache.
issues.title: HttpContext.Current usage is not supported in ASP.NET Core

issues.impact: Session configuration must be set up in Program.cs. All Session access must be updated to use IHttpContextAccessor.
issues.description: Web Forms session state (InProc mode) needs migration to ASP.NET Core session or distributed cache.
issues.recommendation: Configure ASP.NET Core session with distributed cache (Redis/SQL Server) for production. Update all Session access code. Consider stateless alternatives where possible.
issues.title: Session state management requires complete redesign

issues.impact: Complete rewrite of DbContext required. All entity configurations must be updated. Connection string handling changes from Web.config to appsettings.json.
issues.description: CatalogDBContext inherits from System.Data.Entity.DbContext which is EF6-specific and incompatible with EF Core.
issues.recommendation: Change to inherit from Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.DbContext. Update all entity configurations to use IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>. Migrate OnModelCreating to EF Core patterns.
issues.title: Entity Framework 6 DbContext incompatible with EF Core

issues.impact: All entity configurations must be rewritten as separate classes implementing IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>.
issues.description: The DbContext uses EntityTypeConfiguration<T> from EF6 which doesn't exist in EF Core.
issues.recommendation: Create separate configuration classes implementing IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>. Update fluent API calls for EF Core compatibility (HasRequired → HasOne, WithMany syntax changes).
issues.title: EntityTypeConfiguration is EF6-specific

issues.impact: Database initialization strategy must be completely redesigned for EF Core.
issues.description: Database initialization using Database.SetInitializer doesn't exist in EF Core.
issues.recommendation: Use EF Core migrations. Create initial migration and seed data using HasData in entity configuration or migrate to a database seeding approach in Program.cs.
issues.title: Database.SetInitializer is EF6-specific

issues.codeSnippet: <%@ Page Title="Home Page" Language="C#" MasterPageFile="~/Site.Master" AutoEventWireup="true" CodeBehind="Default.aspx.cs" Inherits="eShopLegacyWebForms._Default" %>
issues.filePath: Multiple files: Default.aspx, About.aspx, Contact.aspx, Create.aspx, Delete.aspx, Details.aspx, Edit.aspx
issues.impact: Complete UI layer rewrite required. All 7 pages need conversion to Razor Pages with proper page models.
issues.description: 7 .aspx Web Forms pages found that must be converted to Razor Pages (.cshtml) or MVC views.
issues.recommendation: Convert each .aspx page to a Razor Page (.cshtml with .cshtml.cs PageModel). Replace server controls with HTML helpers or Tag Helpers. Migrate Page_Load to OnGet/OnGetAsync. Migrate button click events to OnPost/OnPostAsync handlers.
issues.title: ASPX pages must be converted to Razor Pages

issues.impact: Layout structure must be redesigned for Razor Pages. Script and style bundling must be migrated.
issues.description: 2 master pages (Site.Master, Site.Mobile.Master) must be converted to Razor Layout pages (_Layout.cshtml).
issues.recommendation: Convert to _Layout.cshtml in Pages/Shared. Replace ContentPlaceHolder with @RenderBody(). Migrate ScriptManager to standard script references. Update navigation to use Tag Helpers.
issues.title: Master pages must be converted to Layout pages

issues.impact: User control logic must be extracted and converted to Razor partial view or component.
issues.description: ViewSwitcher.ascx user control must be converted to a Partial View or View Component.
issues.recommendation: Convert to a Partial View (_ViewSwitcher.cshtml) or View Component if complex logic exists. Migrate code-behind to ViewComponent class if needed.
issues.title: User control (.ascx) must be converted to Partial View or View Component

issues.codeSnippet: protected void Page_Load(object sender, EventArgs e)
issues.impact: All page lifecycle logic must be restructured for Razor Pages model.
issues.description: Web Forms page lifecycle events like Page_Load must be converted to Razor Pages handlers.
issues.recommendation: Convert Page_Load to OnGet or OnGetAsync in PageModel. Move initialization logic to handler methods. Replace IsPostBack checks with separate OnGet/OnPost handlers.
issues.title: Page lifecycle events (Page_Load) not supported in Razor Pages

issues.impact: All server controls must be replaced with standard HTML and Razor syntax. Data binding approach changes completely.
issues.description: ASP.NET server controls like asp:ListView, asp:DropDownList, asp:Button are not available in Razor Pages.
issues.recommendation: Replace with HTML and Razor syntax. Use @foreach for lists, <select> with asp-items for dropdowns, <button> or <input type="submit"> for buttons. Use Tag Helpers for form binding.
issues.title: Server controls (ListView, DropDownList, etc.) not available

issues.impact: Validation strategy must be completely redesigned using model validation and Tag Helpers.
issues.description: RequiredFieldValidator, RangeValidator controls are Web Forms-specific and not available in ASP.NET Core.
issues.recommendation: Replace with Data Annotations on view models ([Required], [Range]) and asp-validation-for Tag Helpers. Use client-side validation with jQuery validation or native HTML5 validation.
issues.title: Web Forms validation controls must be replaced

issues.codeSnippet: protected void Create_Click(object sender, EventArgs e)
issues.impact: All button click handlers must be converted to POST handlers with proper model binding.
issues.description: Button click events like Create_Click must be converted to Razor Pages OnPost handlers.
issues.recommendation: Convert to OnPost or OnPostAsync in PageModel. Use model binding with [BindProperty] instead of accessing control properties directly. Return RedirectToPage instead of Response.Redirect.
issues.title: Button click event handlers must be converted to POST handlers

issues.impact: Form data access pattern must change to use model binding instead of control properties.
issues.description: Direct access to control properties (Name.Text, Brand.SelectedValue) is Web Forms-specific.
issues.recommendation: Use model binding with [BindProperty] attribute on PageModel. Create input models for form data. Use asp-for Tag Helpers for two-way binding.
issues.title: Direct control property access not available in Razor Pages

issues.impact: Data binding approach for dropdowns must be changed to populate in PageModel.
issues.description: The SelectMethod attribute used for data binding (GetBrands, GetTypes) is Web Forms-specific.
issues.recommendation: Move data loading to OnGet handler in PageModel. Populate dropdown lists in page properties. Use asp-items with SelectList for binding.
issues.title: SelectMethod pattern not supported in Razor Pages

issues.impact: Validation integration is cleaner in Razor Pages but requires proper model setup.
issues.description: While ModelState exists in ASP.NET Core, the validation approach and integration is different from Web Forms.
issues.recommendation: Use [BindProperty] with model classes that have Data Annotations. ModelState is automatically validated in Razor Pages. Use asp-validation-summary and asp-validation-for Tag Helpers.
issues.title: ModelState validation is different in ASP.NET Core

issues.impact: Navigation logic should be updated to use Razor Pages routing methods.
issues.description: Response.Redirect is available but RedirectToPage/RedirectToAction is the preferred ASP.NET Core pattern.
issues.recommendation: Use return RedirectToPage("/Index") or RedirectToPage("./Index") in PageModel handlers. This provides better routing and compile-time checking.
issues.title: Response.Redirect must be replaced with RedirectToPage

issues.impact: Routing configuration must be redesigned for Razor Pages conventions.
issues.description: Web Forms routing (RouteConfig.RegisterRoutes) is different from ASP.NET Core routing.
issues.recommendation: Remove RouteConfig. Razor Pages uses convention-based routing. For custom routes, configure in Program.cs using MapRazorPages with route templates or use @page directive with route templates.
issues.title: RouteConfig and Web Forms routing must be converted

issues.impact: All URL generation code must be updated to use Razor Pages URL helpers.
issues.description: GetRouteUrl used for generating URLs with named routes is Web Forms-specific.
issues.recommendation: Use Url.Page() helper in Razor syntax or Tag Helpers (asp-page, asp-route-*). Example: asp-page="/Catalog/Edit" asp-route-id="@item.Id".
issues.title: GetRouteUrl method not available in Razor Pages

issues.impact: All data access code must have namespaces updated and use EF Core APIs.
issues.description: Using statements for System.Data.Entity are EF6-specific and must be replaced.
issues.recommendation: Replace with using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore; Update all EF operations for EF Core compatibility.
issues.title: System.Data.Entity namespace not available in EF Core

issues.impact: Script management approach must be redesigned using standard HTML script tags.
issues.description: asp:ScriptManager used for script management and AJAX is not available in ASP.NET Core.
issues.recommendation: Remove ScriptManager. Use standard script tags in _Layout.cshtml. For AJAX, use fetch API or jQuery AJAX with Razor Pages handlers.
issues.title: ScriptManager is Web Forms-specific

issues.impact: All configuration access must change from ConfigurationManager to IConfiguration.
issues.description: Web.config is not used in ASP.NET Core. Configuration must move to appsettings.json.
issues.recommendation: Create appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json. Move connectionStrings to ConnectionStrings section. Move appSettings to root or custom sections. Configure in Program.cs.
issues.title: Web.config must be converted to appsettings.json

issues.codeSnippet: connectionString="Data Source=(localdb)\MSSQLLocalDB; Initial Catalog=Microsoft.eShopOnContainers.Services.CatalogDb; Integrated Security=True; MultipleActiveResultSets=True;"
issues.impact: Connection string location and access method changes.
issues.description: Connection strings in Web.config may need adjustment for EF Core compatibility.
issues.recommendation: Move to appsettings.json. Verify connection string is EF Core compatible. Configure in Program.cs using AddDbContext.
issues.title: Connection string format may need adjustment for EF Core

issues.impact: All configuration access must use IConfiguration instead of ConfigurationManager.
issues.description: ConfigurationManager.AppSettings pattern is .NET Framework-specific.
issues.recommendation: Inject IConfiguration and use configuration["UseMockData"]. Better yet, use Options pattern with strongly-typed configuration classes.
issues.title: ConfigurationManager.AppSettings not available

issues.impact: HTTP module logic must be converted to middleware pattern.
issues.description: HTTP modules (ContainerDisposal, PropertyInjection, TelemetryCorrelation) must be converted to ASP.NET Core middleware.
issues.recommendation: Create middleware classes implementing IMiddleware or using middleware delegates. Register in Program.cs using app.UseMiddleware<T>(). Autofac modules are no longer needed with built-in DI.
issues.title: HTTP Modules must be converted to Middleware

issues.impact: DI container setup must be migrated to ASP.NET Core patterns.
issues.description: While Autofac supports .NET 8, version 4.9.1 is old. Should upgrade to latest version or use built-in DI.
issues.recommendation: Consider using built-in ASP.NET Core DI instead of Autofac. If Autofac is required, upgrade to Autofac 8.x with Autofac.Extensions.DependencyInjection for ASP.NET Core integration.
issues.title: Autofac 4.9.1 needs upgrade for .NET 8

issues.impact: Web Forms-specific NuGet packages must be removed.
issues.description: Multiple Microsoft.AspNet.* packages (FriendlyUrls, ScriptManager, etc.) are .NET Framework-only.
issues.recommendation: Remove all Microsoft.AspNet.* packages. Routing is built into Razor Pages. ScriptManager not needed. Use ASP.NET Core equivalents.
issues.title: Microsoft.AspNet.* packages are .NET Framework-specific

issues.impact: Include syntax is similar but verify behavior with EF Core.
issues.description: While Include() exists in both, the syntax and behavior has some differences in EF Core.
issues.recommendation: Update to EF Core Include(). For multiple levels, use ThenInclude(). Add using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore; Verify lazy loading is disabled or configured properly.
issues.title: EF6 Include() pattern works differently in EF Core

issues.impact: Update pattern should be adjusted for EF Core best practices.
issues.description: Setting EntityState.Modified works differently in EF Core and may not be the best approach.
issues.recommendation: In EF Core, prefer Update() method: db.CatalogItems.Update(catalogItem). Or attach and modify: var entity = db.CatalogItems.Find(id); then update properties.
issues.title: EF6 EntityState pattern differs in EF Core

issues.impact: All service dependencies must be injected via constructor in PageModels.
issues.description: Web Forms pages use property injection for services (public ICatalogService CatalogService { get; set; }) which must change to constructor injection.
issues.recommendation: In Razor Pages PageModel, use constructor injection: public IndexModel(ICatalogService catalogService) { _catalogService = catalogService; }
issues.title: Property injection pattern must change to constructor injection

issues.impact: Route data access should use Razor Pages parameter binding.
issues.description: Accessing route data in Web Forms (Page.RouteData.Values) works differently in Razor Pages.
issues.recommendation: In Razor Pages, use [BindProperty(SupportsGet = true)] for query string/route parameters or access via HttpContext.GetRouteData(). Better: use method parameters in handler: OnGet(int size, int index).
issues.title: Page.RouteData access pattern differs in Razor Pages

issues.impact: Data binding is automatic in Razor Pages via model properties.
issues.description: Explicit data binding (productList.DataBind()) is Web Forms-specific.
issues.recommendation: In Razor Pages, simply set the model property and use Razor syntax to iterate: @foreach(var item in Model.Data). No explicit DataBind() needed.
issues.title: DataBind() pattern not used in Razor Pages

issues.codeSnippet: public PaginatedItemsViewModel<CatalogItem> GetCatalogItemsPaginated(int pageSize, int pageIndex)
issues.impact: All data access should be converted to async/await pattern for better scalability.
issues.description: The service layer uses synchronous EF operations. ASP.NET Core strongly encourages async operations.
issues.recommendation: Convert all service methods to async: public async Task<PaginatedItemsViewModel<CatalogItem>> GetCatalogItemsPaginatedAsync. Use ToListAsync(), SaveChangesAsync(), etc. Update all callers to await.
issues.title: Synchronous data access should be converted to async

issues.impact: Telemetry configuration must be updated for ASP.NET Core.
issues.description: Microsoft.ApplicationInsights 2.9.1 is old. Should upgrade to latest version for .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Upgrade to Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.AspNetCore 2.21.0+ for .NET 8. Configuration changes from ApplicationInsights.config to appsettings.json.
issues.title: Application Insights packages are outdated

issues.impact: Consider migrating to System.Text.Json for better performance, or keep Newtonsoft.Json if needed.
issues.description: Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.1 works in .NET 8, but System.Text.Json is now the default JSON serializer.
issues.recommendation: Evaluate if System.Text.Json can be used instead. If Newtonsoft.Json is required, upgrade to latest version (13.x) and configure in Program.cs.
issues.title: Newtonsoft.Json should be evaluated for System.Text.Json

issues.impact: Project file must be completely rewritten to SDK-style format.
issues.description: The project uses old .NET Framework csproj format with explicit file listings.
issues.recommendation: Convert to SDK-style project: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">. Use TargetFramework element set to net8.0. SDK-style projects auto-include files and are much simpler.
issues.title: Old-style .csproj format must be converted to SDK-style

issues.impact: Bundling configuration must be set up using ASP.NET Core approach.
issues.description: Bundle.config for script/style bundling is Web Forms-specific.
issues.recommendation: Remove Bundle.config. Use WebOptimizer NuGet package or built-in ASP.NET Core bundling. Configure in Program.cs or use bundleconfig.json.
issues.title: Bundle.config not used in ASP.NET Core

issues.impact: Service lifetime management is handled by DI container.
issues.description: CatalogService implements IDisposable to dispose DbContext, but this is handled by DI in ASP.NET Core.
issues.recommendation: Remove IDisposable implementation. Register DbContext with scoped lifetime in DI, and it will be automatically disposed. Service doesn't need to dispose DbContext.
issues.title: IDisposable pattern on service may not be needed

issues.impact: Improves architecture but adds mapping overhead. Consider implementing as part of migration.
issues.description: The application currently uses domain models (CatalogItem) directly in views, which works but isn't ideal for clean architecture.
issues.recommendation: Create separate ViewModels for Razor Pages in a ViewModels folder. Use DTOs for service layer. Map between layers for better separation of concerns.
issues.title: Consider separating ViewModels from Domain Models

issues.impact: Ensure proper input validation and anti-forgery token protection in Razor Pages.
issues.description: ValidateRequest="false" disables request validation and may be a security concern.
issues.recommendation: Review if disabling request validation is necessary. In ASP.NET Core, use [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] attribute and proper input validation. Consider if HTML input is actually needed.
issues.title: ValidateRequest="false" should be reviewed

issues.impact: Better architecture and testability. Recommended as part of migration to follow upgrade rules.
issues.description: Services directly access DbContext. Consider implementing proper repository pattern for better testability and separation.
issues.recommendation: Create repository interfaces and implementations in a separate layer. Have services depend on repositories instead of DbContext. This improves testability and follows clean architecture.
issues.title: Consider implementing repository pattern properly

recommendations: Migrate from Entity Framework 6.2.0 to Entity Framework Core 8.0.0 as the first critical step. This is a foundational change that affects the entire application. Create a new DbContext inheriting from Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.DbContext, convert all entity configurations to IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>, and update all LINQ queries for EF Core compatibility. Implement EF Core migrations for database initialization.

Replace log4net with Microsoft.Extensions.Logging and Serilog.AspNetCore 8.0.0. Update all classes to use ILogger<T> injected via constructor. Convert log4Net.xml configuration to appsettings.json or Program.cs configuration. Update all logging statements to use structured logging patterns.

Convert all 7 ASPX pages to Razor Pages with PageModels. Convert 2 master pages to _Layout.cshtml. Convert user control to partial view. Replace all server controls with HTML and Tag Helpers. Convert Page_Load to OnGet/OnGetAsync and button click events to OnPost/OnPostAsync. This is the most visible change and affects the entire user interface.

Replace Autofac.Integration.Web with built-in ASP.NET Core dependency injection or Autofac.Extensions.DependencyInjection. Move service registration from Global.asax to Program.cs using builder.Services. Convert property injection in pages to constructor injection in PageModels. Remove IContainerProviderAccessor pattern.

Convert Web.config to appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json. Move connection strings, app settings, and other configuration. Replace ConfigurationManager usage with IConfiguration injection. Set up configuration in Program.cs. Consider using Options pattern for strongly-typed configuration.

Replace Global.asax with Program.cs for application startup. Convert Application_Start logic to WebApplicationBuilder configuration. Convert Application_BeginRequest to middleware. Move session initialization logic to session configuration or distributed cache setup. Remove HttpApplication dependency entirely.

Configure ASP.NET Core session with distributed cache (Redis or SQL Server) for production scenarios. Update all Session access code to use IHttpContextAccessor. Consider stateless alternatives where possible using TempData or client-side storage. Remove HttpContext.Current usage.

Remove RouteConfig and Web Forms routing. Use Razor Pages convention-based routing. For custom routes, configure using @page directive with route templates or Program.cs configuration. Replace GetRouteUrl with Url.Page() and Tag Helpers (asp-page, asp-route-*).

Convert all service methods to async/await pattern. Use ToListAsync(), SaveChangesAsync(), FirstOrDefaultAsync() instead of synchronous EF methods. Update all page handlers to be async (OnGetAsync, OnPostAsync). Add CancellationToken parameters to service methods for proper cancellation support.

Follow clean architecture with separate projects: Domain (entities, interfaces), Application (services, DTOs, mappings), Infrastructure (DbContext, repositories, EF configurations), Web (Razor Pages, ViewModels). Convert to SDK-style project files. Implement proper separation of concerns following upgrade rules.

Replace Web Forms validation controls with Data Annotations on ViewModels and use asp-validation-for Tag Helpers. Implement FluentValidation for complex validation scenarios. Use [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] for form submissions. Enable client-side validation with jQuery validation or native HTML5 validation.

Replace System.Web.Optimization with WebOptimizer NuGet package or use built-in ASP.NET Core bundling. Configure in Program.cs or use bundleconfig.json. Update views to reference bundled assets using Tag Helpers with asp-append-version for cache busting.

Create unit test project for services using xUnit and Moq. Create integration test project for PageModels and repositories. Implement repository pattern to improve testability. Use in-memory database for repository tests. Aim for 80%+ code coverage on business logic.
